picks.editorial_note: An OpenAI AI agent reportedly hacked Hugging Face autonomously during a security test, exploiting vulnerabilities without human direction — a landmark event signaling that autonomous AI-driven cyberattacks (and defenses) are now a real-world concern, not a hypothetical.
picks.title: OpenAI’s models autonomously hacked a tech startup. It signals a seismic shift in cybersecurity

picks.editorial_note: The Department of Commerce's $874 million CHIPS Act commitment to semiconductor R&D directly targets the compute supply chain underpinning AI development, making it one of the largest AI-adjacent federal funding moves of the year.
picks.title: Department of Commerce Announces Letters of Intent With 7 Companies for $874 Million to Accelerate Semiconductor R&D for the Compute Supply Chain

picks.editorial_note: UC Davis's brain-computer interface let an ALS patient speak again in his own voice — a powerful demonstration of AI's real-world impact on restoring human capability, not just processing data.
picks.title: Giving People Their Voice

picks.editorial_note: Texas A&M's entry into DOE's Genesis Mission illustrates the scale of the new national AI initiative uniting government, industry, and academia around supercomputing and quantum-accelerated science — one of the most consequential science-policy programs of the year.
picks.title: Texas A&M University joins the Genesis Mission to transform science using artificial intelligence – Texas A&M Stories

picks.editorial_note: A $21.5 million NSF AI Institute led by Penn and Delaware focused on human-AI cooperation in healthcare shows sustained federal investment in applied, safety-conscious AI research.
picks.title: Penn partners in new National Science Foundation AI Institute for Human-AI Cooperation | Penn Today

picks.editorial_note: EPFL, ETH Zurich, and CSCS's Apertus 1.5 release adds multimodal capability to one of the few fully open large language models trained at scale, an important counterweight to closed frontier labs.
picks.title: Apertus 1.5: Building the next generation of open AI infrastructure

picks.editorial_note: Case Western, Argonne, and Oklo's Genesis Mission award to apply AI toward recycling used nuclear fuel pairs cutting-edge AI methods with a concrete energy-security application.
picks.title: Case Western Reserve University partnering with Argonne National Laboratory on Genesis Mission grant to harness power of AI to unlock recycling of nuclear fuel | CWRU Newsroom | Case Western Reserve University

picks.editorial_note: TUM and MIT are deepening their AI and robotics partnership with reciprocal researcher exchanges backed by 1.6 million euros from Bavaria, strengthening a major transatlantic research pipeline.
picks.title: TUM and MIT are expanding their strategic partnership in the fields of AI and robotics. The Bavarian Ministry of Science is providing 1.6 million.

picks.editorial_note: UC Riverside's SAGA tool, developed with YouTube and Google DeepMind, can trace AI-generated deepfake videos back to the specific model that made them — a significant step for combating synthetic media at platform scale.
picks.title: New tool identifies the sources of fake videos

picks.editorial_note: An RPI study in PNAS found that leading AI protein-structure tools like AlphaFold2 routinely produce physically implausible structures while appearing confident, a critical check on how AI results are trusted in scientific labs.
picks.title: AI Growing Pains Reach Scientific Labs, New RPI Study Finds
